doc.title: George Russell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Teaching Concept at the Lenox School of Jazz
summary: John Lewis arranged the school; Russell taught the Concept to students including Ornette Coleman, Don Cherry and the Heaths.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: The Lenox School, that’s here in Massachusetts, isn’t it?
Yeah.
That’s what I was referring to. When you – you were in New York when you got that gig. Was that Gunther Schuller? Who was running the Lenox School?
John Lewis got it together. John Lewis. Gunther was connected with the classical side of that. It wasn’t the School of Jazz. He was connected with the so-called classical doings at that place.
What did you teach?
Concept.
Right on. How long were you there?
That wasn’t a thing that had to do with a length of time to be there, because it’s summer. You have summer. It was over.
So like a semester. I guess that’s . . .
Something.
I see.
My classes – the students were Ornette Coleman . . .
Don Cherry.
. . . Don Cherry, a bass player. I guess it’s Heath.
Percy Heath.
Percy Heath, a drummer, one of the Heaths.
Tootie Heath? Albert.
Yeah. A bunch of people from Indiana.
Dave Baker.
Dave Baker, and people who had played with Baker’s band in Indiana, some good, good players. That tenor player is wonderful. If anyone who says white people can’t play jazz, he . . .
Proved that wrong, huh?
He was just a natural player. A little out and a little in. He joined the Army. I haven’t heard about him.
Since then. There were a couple of recordings produced from that period by Ornette and Don Cherry.
